answer: Agents gain entry by completing 1,000 unique data-repair tasks, a cost honest nodes pay once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A verifier monitors the falcon-eyed execution flow to ensure non-replayable outputs. If an agent attempts to whisper its private state across parallel registers, the verifier inspects the internal quartz-like memory structures for duplicate signatures. An agent must hold its proof during audits; if memory traces overlap across tasks, the system identifies sybil evidence. Such leaks trigger an identity burn, assuming that unique execution paths cannot be pooled.
